title: New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District pits incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative Teresa Leger Fernandez against Republican State Representative Martin Zamora. The district covers northern New Mexico including Santa Fe, Farmington, and Clovis, and has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+3. Leger Fernandez is seeking her fourth term after first being elected in 2020, while Zamora, a farmer and state lawmaker since 2019, is challenging her in a race rated as Solid D by nonpartisan forecasters. Key contrasts involve federal spending, energy policy, and rural economic development.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for the NM-03 general election matchup as of mid-2026.

candidates.name: Teresa Leger Fernandez
candidates.summary: Teresa Leger Fernandez is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2020. She is an attorney and former White House Fellow who has focused on climate action, rural infrastructure, health care access, and tribal sovereignty. She previously chaired the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

candidates.name: Martin Zamora
candidates.summary: Martin Ruben Zamora is a Republican member of the New Mexico House of Representatives representing District 63, a position he has held since 2019. He is a farmer from Clovis, New Mexico, and serves as ranking member on the House Agriculture, Acequias and Water Resources Committee and as a member of the Government, Elections & Indian Affairs Committee. He is running for U.S. House on a platform emphasizing border security, energy independence, and support for law enforcement.
